lead.headline: Visa adds Monad to stablecoin settlement stack as banks commit $270M to rival Project Faro
lead.tldr: Traditional finance is building on two tracks simultaneously: incumbent networks integrating public-chain infrastructure while banks pool capital for captive alternatives. The tension between these approaches is becoming the central pricing question for stablecoin infrastructure.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today the signals point to a race between integration and enclosure in stablecoin infrastructure, with security failures on the margins reminding us what still breaks.

top_signals.title: Global banks commit $270M to stablecoin venture targeting 2027 launch
top_signals.summary: Global banks have committed $270 million to Project Faro to develop a bank-issued dollar stablecoin slated for a 2027 launch. While the project has significant backing, some participating members are simultaneously supporting competing stablecoin initiatives.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $270M Project Faro commitment reveals banks hedging between collective stablecoin issuance and fragmented competitive strategies, which complicates any attempt to underwrite the sector on network effects alone.

top_signals.title: Visa adds Monad to stablecoin settlement network options
top_signals.summary: Visa has integrated Monad into its stablecoin settlement network, allowing issuers and acquirers to utilize the protocol for transactions. The partnership will expand to include privacy features in the near future.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Visa's Monad integration signals that major payment networks now treat public-chain settlement as table stakes, repricing the infrastructure layer away from proprietary rails toward protocol-level competition.

top_signals.title: Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip
top_signals.summary: Crypto advocate Tom Emmer has been elected as the House Republican minority whip. This places a pro-digital asset lawmaker in a senior leadership position within the GOP.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Emmer's elevation to House GOP whip places crypto policy advocacy inside leadership scheduling and vote-counting, which matters less for immediate legislation than for signaling where Republican capital will flow in 2025.

top_signals.title: LNbits rushes emergency patch after reported Bitcoin wallet thefts
top_signals.summary: LNbits has issued an emergency security patch following reports of Bitcoin thefts from its Lightning wallet software. Users are urged to update their software immediately and reset their credentials to secure their funds.
top_signals.why_it_matters: LNbits' emergency patch underscores that Lightning infrastructure remains brittle enough to require credential resets at scale, a liability for any payment stack underwriting Bitcoin's retail layer.

top_signals.title: Across Protocol warns users to avoid app amid reports of drained wallets37m
top_signals.summary: Across Protocol has issued an urgent warning to its users to avoid using its application following reports of drained wallets. The protocol is investigating the cause of the security breach to protect remaining user funds.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Across Protocol's wallet drainage incident, following LNbits within hours, suggests either coordinated targeting or systemic tooling vulnerabilities that should raise due diligence thresholds for cross-chain infrastructure.

deals.summary: Alta has raised $47.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Index Ventures. The company is developing a specialized blockchain tailored for use by financial institutions.

Securitize, backed by BlackRock, has agreed to acquire River One to expand its capabilities into the asset-backed lending market. This move targets a sector estimated to be worth approximately $6 trillion.

on_the_radar.title: Polymarket US trading volume jumps 266% despite regulatory battles
on_the_radar.summary: Polymarket saw a massive 266% increase in US trading volume during October, reaching $14.77 billion. This growth occurred despite ongoing legal and regulatory disputes regarding the oversight of prediction markets.

on_the_radar.title: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures28m, Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futuresCoinbase, Kalshi and four other companies backed the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks.
on_the_radar.summary: Coinbase and Kalshi have joined a lawsuit supporting the CFTC regarding the legality of US exchanges listing perpetual futures tied to individual stocks. The case centers on regulatory jurisdiction and the permissibility of these specific financial instruments in the US market.

on_the_radar.title: Binance warns iOS flaw could expose crypto wallet keys3m
on_the_radar.summary: Binance has issued a warning regarding a critical iOS flaw that could potentially expose private keys of cryptocurrency wallets. Users are urged to update their devices to the latest software version to mitigate the security risk.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says
on_the_radar.summary: Security firm CertiK is urging crypto exchanges to implement hard dollar caps on hot wallets to prevent massive losses. This recommendation follows a reported $6.3 billion hack of Binance, highlighting the inadequacy of relying solely on cold-storage ratios.

on_the_radar.title: Forward Industries grows SOL treasury to 8.7 million as token hits nearly three-month low
on_the_radar.summary: Forward Industries has increased its SOL treasury to 8.7 million tokens amid a price dip. The company has also secured a $50 million credit line and committed $50 million to a tokenized U.S. home-price product.

on_the_radar.title: Kimber Digital Securities gains broker-dealer status for tokenized assets
on_the_radar.summary: Kimber Digital Securities has secured SEC broker-dealer registration to facilitate the trading of tokenized assets. The firm plans to offer tokenized US stocks, ETFs, and bonds directly to self-custodial wallets.

on_the_radar.title: Mercado Bitcoin to resume cash withdrawals after $49M hack16m
on_the_radar.summary: Mercado Bitcoin is resuming cash withdrawals for its users following a security breach that resulted in a $49 million loss. The exchange is working to restore full functionality after the hack disrupted operations.

on_the_radar.title: TON Strategy earns $13.1 million from GRAM staking in Q3 as Telegram rolls out native wallet
on_the_radar.summary: TON Strategy generated $13.1 million from GRAM staking during Q3. Simultaneously, Telegram has begun the rollout of its native Gram Wallet to enhance user access to the network.

worth_a_read.note: a16z's agent-networks thesis is worth tracking because it reframes blockchain infrastructure as coordination layers for autonomous economic actors rather than human-readable interfaces, which has implications for which protocols capture value in a post-interface market.

linkedin_post:
Visa adding Monad to its stablecoin settlement network on the same day global banks commit $270 million to Project Faro is not coincidence. It is the two paths we are underwriting now.

One path: incumbent networks plugging public infrastructure into existing flows, letting issuers and acquirers choose their rails. The other: banks building a captive dollar token they control end-to-end, launch date 2027. The same banks, in several cases, are walking both paths simultaneously.

We do not think this means banks are confused. We think it means they have not yet priced which model wins. Visa's integration treats stablecoin settlement as a commodity layer where speed and cost determine routing. Project Faro treats it as a strategic moat where issuer identity and regulatory shelter matter more. Both cannot be right at the same scale.

What would settle it: if a major Faro participant quietly shifts volume to Visa-integrated rails before 2027, the bank consortium thesis starts leaking. If Visa's Monad volume stays thin while Faro builds regulatory lock-in, the enclosure model gets repriced upward.

The security failures today—LNbits, Across—are noise at the margin. The signal is infrastructure providers choosing between open integration and walled gardens. We are watching where the volume actually moves, not where the press releases say it will.
